source_text: Superior de principiis Levitici dictum est; nunc lex sacrificiorum quae munera appellantur. Anima quae peccaverit ex populo — non voluntate semper, sed ignorantia — munus offert. Synagoga et anima typice leguntur.
pass_a_gloss: Earlier about principles of-Leviticus it-has-been-said; now law of-sacrifices which gifts are-called. Soul which will-have-sinned from people — not by-will always, but by-ignorance — gift offers. Synagogue and soul typically are-read.
pass_b_english: We spoke before of Leviticus’s beginnings; now comes the law of sacrifices called [[gifts >> Bible:Leviticus 2:1]]. A soul that sins from among the people — not always willfully, but in ignorance — brings an offering. Synagogue and soul are read as types.
